details:
Our project, Earth Analogues for Permanent Moon Base Locations & Mars, bridges the gap between orbital planetary science and ground-based analog testing. While Earth cannot replicate lunar or Martian surface gravity ($0.16g$ and $0.38g$) or extreme atmospheric vacuums, it does share governing physical, thermal, and chemical processes.

The project operates as a multi-parameter analog matching framework that cross-references terrestrial sites against lunar and Martian targets using specific, high-priority criteria:

  • Iron-Rich Basaltic Mineralogy: Matching volcanic and regolith chemistry.
  • Debris-Covered & Buried Ice: Locating stable sub-surface water reservoirs protected by rocky debris mantles.
  • Topographic & Structural Shelter: Identifying steep slope profiles, impact crater geomorphology, and subterranean cave or lava-tube geometries.

2. Selected Terrestrial Priority Sites

  • Wrangell–St. Elias Mountains, Alaska (Root & Kennicott Glaciers): Serves as a primary terrestrial analog for thick, debris-covered glacial ice that persists safely under a walkable, rocky surface mantle.
  • Khumbu & Langtang Valleys, Nepal: High-altitude debris-mantled glacier systems where 20% to 30% of glacial ice is hidden under thick supraglacial debris, mimicking Martian lobate debris aprons.

3. Core Data Sources & Resources Utilized

Our methodology integrates rigorous multi-agency open data and spatial archives:

  • NASA Data Sources:
    • SWIM Subsurface Ice Map (PIA26045)for mapping underground water-ice consistency.
    • Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) & CTX Topographyfor elevation models and crater morphology.
    • PDS Geosciences Archivesfor mission datasets including LRO, GRAIL, LCROSS, CLPS, and MSX.
    • NSIDC HMA2_DCG_SMB(High Mountain Asia DEMs and mass balance data for Khumbu/Langtang valleys).
    • ITS_LIVE ice velocity datasetsfor analyzing glacial flow dynamics.

4. Solution Concept & Innovation

Beyond a static database, the project proposes a multi-parameter interactive analog matcher allowing researchers and planners to toggle filters for regolith chemistry, slope angle, ice proximity, and structural shelter.

Additionally, we propose an industrial $\text{CO}_2$-capture test-shell concept co-located with basaltic terrain as a practical, ground-based atmospheric proxy for testing life-support and resource utilization systems under harsh conditions.

5. Intended Impact & Benefits

By establishing a rigorous, process-driven terrestrial matching system, this project optimizes the selection of analog testing grounds for future robotic mobility rovers, human habitat construction, in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) technology, and long-term survival infrastructure.
